summary_paragraph: A woman with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and history of chronic cyclic nausea with dry heaves and poor solid-food tolerance was admitted to the surgical service after planned Interventional Radiology gastrostomy tube placement to transition from TPN to enteral nutrition for protein-calorie malnutrition. Post-procedure she tolerated clear liquids, then after 24 hours started tube feeds that were advanced to goal and cycled for home use, with improvement in nausea and tolerance of a regular diet as able. Pain was limited to mild tube-site discomfort controlled with oral medication; she remained afebrile and hemodynamically stable without infectious complications. She was discharged home with services on goal tube feeds and free-water flushes, with PICC removed and instructions for tube-site care and return precautions.
